info.title: Plyback
info.description: Plyback native server. Password sessions and X-Requested-With: plyback protect API requests.

get.description: The account’s reviewed games for one colour as a move tree from the standard start: games, score, book and left-book counts per move, and error counts for the account’s own moves, the named opening and up to three recent game IDs (and plies) per move, plus up to eight problem moves. Each node has `from` and `to` position ids (`root` is the start), so a client can walk the tree in either mode.

parameters.name: merge
parameters.description: Group moves by the position they were played from, so move orders that transpose share statistics. Each node is listed under its most common move order.

get.description: Due positions first, then new ones from the most recent games. Positions are the account’s own blunders, mistakes and misses in standard chess whose best move beats the second engine line by at least 0.05 expected points. The answer is only returned after an attempt. Themes are derived from the stored best line without new engine searches. Clients should show item themes only after solving, skipping or revealing a puzzle.

parameters.name: theme
parameters.description: Restrict the queue and its statistics to positions with this tactical theme. Empty or all includes every theme and untagged positions.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Unix time. When set, every position from games that ended since then, answered or not, in random order.

post.description: Send {"uci": "e2e4"} to answer, or {"reveal": true} to show the answer (counts as a miss). Returns whether it was correct, the solution and the new schedule. The solution includes the same derived themes as the queue item.
Set, change or remove the access password. Changing or removing needs the current one.

parameters.name: ending
parameters.description: How a decisive game ended: checkmate, resignation, time or abandoned.

TacticalTheme.description: Conservatively detected from the puzzle position and its stored best line; a puzzle can have no themes.

themes.description: Hidden in the interface until the puzzle is solved, skipped or revealed.

stats.description: Totals and scheduling statistics after all requested filters.

theme_counts.description: One count per supported theme, including zero. Counts include scheduled positions, respect kind, phase and since, and are computed before the theme filter and queue limit. Multi-theme puzzles count once in each applicable theme.
